capturedAgainst: confidence-gated selector: trust multifeature when conf >= 0.5, else percival; no octave/fine-tune/snap chain

syntheticComparison.note: Three-way comparison over the octave-widened synthetic set (23 cases, 44.1kHz). This is what settled the 'delete the tempo ensemble' question: removing the octave-normalized averaging is a real gain, but deleting the octave selector on top of it regresses by 8.7 points. Measured, not reasoned. Reproduce via the 'Algorithm Comparison' suite with RUN_INTEGRATION_TESTS=true.
syntheticComparison.warning: These synthetic numbers were measured on `drumPattern` fixtures whose onsets-per-second is exactly 2 x (bpm/60) — a deterministic function of tempo — which makes density-based octave logic correct by construction. They are RETAINED AS A CAUTIONARY RECORD, not as evidence. On `tempoRealistic` fixtures and on real audio the ordering reverses. Do not cite the 82.6% figure.

caveat: Synthetic Accuracy2 reaches 100%, implying errors are octave-only. Real audio does NOT agree: the tapped-ground-truth rows above show Accuracy2 of 60%, with 150-vs-71 and 188-vs-75 failures that are not octave relationships. Synthetic fixtures under-represent genuine beat-tracking failure. Do not tune octave policy on synthetic numbers alone.

beforeAfter.note: Real tapped-library measurement across the whole change. Accuracy1 quadrupled and every invented output disappeared. The winning combination needed all three pieces; any two of them measured no better than the original.

openGap: White Flag (truth 160) reads 84. NO estimator proposes 160 — multifeature/degara/degara-clip all say 172.3 and percival says 85.1. Either it is a genuinely hard track or the tap is off. It is the one remaining failure and it is not an octave error. n=5 remains thin; the threshold should be re-derived, not assumed, as more songs are tapped.
howItWasDerived: Not tuned by trial. Per-estimator BPM AND confidence were captured on the five tapped songs, and multifeature's own confidence separated its correct readings from its wrong ones with a clean gap: correct at 0.667/0.719, wrong at 0.352/0.428/0.053. The threshold 0.5 sits inside that gap. The mechanism is principled rather than fitted — RhythmExtractor2013 derives confidence from agreement among its internal onset-detection functions, so low confidence genuinely means 'my own detectors disagreed', which is when its metrical level is least trustworthy. `percival` is the fallback because it is independent (autocorrelation, not an onset-DF ensemble) and held the correct level in exactly those cases (70.1 vs truth 71; 75.4 vs 75).
